Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I am Nita Anjaikan from the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.

Key details

  • In this lecture, we will look at the concept of functions.
  • We will look at how to define functions, what exactly functions are, and how we could call or use them.
  • It may seem like a bunch of jargon to you, but let me put it in a simpler way.
  • When you have a set of code that say would be used multiple times in your program, rather than copying or repeating those lines of code multiple times, I would rather club all those reusable lines together, put a name for it.
  • Functions ideally would take an input, performs a specific set of operations, and computes and results gives you an output.
  • We are actually familiar with this concept as we have seen in the first unit when we talked about your input and output functions.
  • It takes an input, processes your input, does a couple of steps, and then returns an output.
  • There are different kinds of functions available in Python.
  • You have built in an existing functions like the print and input function, and there are user defined functions which as a programmer we can create based on the needs of our application.
  • What are the advantages of using functions?
  • They are, like I've already said, it reduces the duplication of code by just call the name of the function.
  • It supports modularity, which means that every feature of the application that you build could be a function.
  • It improves the clarity of code because it's so neatly structured as you will see in our examples that you can easily debug the code.
  • It promotes reuse, it enhances readability, and the debugging and maintenance also becomes easier because when that there is a problem with a specific feature, you can directly jump to the lines of code where the function is defined and debug the code appropriately.
  • So in our programming term when we say function definition, it means that we're going to try and create the function.
  • Followed by the name of the function.
  • A function name is an identifier, which means it should start with alphabets, then followed by a number or letter in English, or a digit, followed by a pair of round parentheses and then a colon.
  • It is to give an input to the function if required.
  • We will look at all of that in the upcoming lectures.
  • Once we have and the leader with a colon, you can then use an indented block called the suite, which can have any valid statement in Python.
  • It could be one or more statements, or it could also be another function, as we will see.
  • As you can see, there is define the name of a function followed by a pair of parentheses and the parameters are optional.
  • Then you have an indented block which would be the suite of the program.
  • We must note that a function must be defined before we use or call the function.

Example or application from the lecture

  • So first let's explore at what a function really is.
  • there would be a leader and a suite because we are going to have multiple lines of code that are going to be clubbed and given a single name.
  • So let's just look at an example.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

I know this is a redundant example, but it's just to show you how exactly it works.

Key details

  • Every leader must end with a semicolon.
  • Command prompt and I'm going to execute functions.py, which is the file in which I have written the code.
  • You can see there is no output because all I have done is create the function.
  • I have not brought the function to life.
  • Followed by what we would call a function call operator.
  • Invoke or we would activate the function.
  • So when a function is defined, as you saw that when I executed, I did not get any output because the header or the leader is processed.
  • By using the function call.
  • At that point of time the control is shifted to the entire function block.
  • The function is processed.
  • And there was no output.
  • It goes on to the next set of statements.
  • Before display, I'm going to say print before function call.
  • And after display print after function call.

Example or application from the lecture

  • So let's look at another example where I'm going to like we've shown in this particular PPT, I'm going to create the same display function and have multiple print statements to show you what exactly would happen if I have other statements and what exactly the name of the function actually means.
  • So this example is just to prove that.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

The first two lines are not executed in the beginning.

Key details

  • It's always going to be before and in between the before and after function call.
  • You can see it says it is a function display at a particular location.
  • This is because it's stored in the global memory, right?
  • Which means your function is actually.
  • just another object which has a property to be reused.
  • What does this statement mean?
  • Since the function is an object, I can assign one function object to another.
  • I'm going to write display1 and the function call parameter.
  • Heading over to the interpreter.
  • So when you look at print display and print display one, you can see that both of them are functions at the same location, which means the name of a function is a function object or a variable which is basically a whose value is a function and that can be activated using a pair of round parentheses.
  • Does this delete my function altogether?
  • So if I were to now just call display in the next line, okay I'm going to save it.
  • Head over to the terminal and execute it, you can say I get an error saying the name display is not defined.
  • That's because I have deleted the display function here.
  • After this I'm going to write display1 with the function call.
  • Will this work?
  • It works as expected.
  • I can call it using either one of them.
  • Associated with the function.
  • It doesn't delete the function itself, which means I have display one also pointing to the same function.
  • I hope you have understood the concept.
  • In the upcoming videos, we will look at what exactly happens when a function is called, how we could give input to the function.
  • and process these values as well.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let's look at it.
  • Infer from this particular example is that display and display one are just names for that function object in the memory.
  • So let's look at the next set of information in the upcoming class.
